title: Large Bricks and Join-irreducible torsionfree classes

predicted_errors.error_location: Proposition 3.9, construction of the directed system from a spanning tree
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof chooses a spanning tree T of the Hasse quiver and then asserts: 'This gives a directed system of f-simples consisting of monomorphisms (we don't have any compatibility condition to check on the maps as the underlying graph is a tree).' A subquiver of a Hasse quiver whose underlying graph is a tree need not be a directed system/filtered colimit: edges may have mixed orientations, and pairs of vertices need not have a common upper bound inside the tree. In particular, for a join-irreducible but not completely join-irreducible torsionfree class, Corollary 2.11 gives an f-simple poset of infinite height, necessarily without a maximum, so such a spanning tree cannot generally be a directed poset. Lemma 3.6 requires a direct system (filtered colimit), so it does not apply to an arbitrary tree diagram. Moreover, a colimit of a tree diagram of monomorphisms is not necessarily in lim→ f (e.g. a pushout of two f-simples along a common submodule can leave f). Thus the main proof is invalid as written.

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 3.6, proof that every proper quotient of F is torsion
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says: 'Using the fact that torsion classes are closed under quotients, this task can be reduced to proving that every maximal quotient of F is a torsion module.' This implication is false: a module can have all its simple quotients in a torsion class without itself being torsion. For example, over the path algebra of 1→2, the torsion class add(S1) has simple quotient S1; the module P1 has unique simple quotient S1 ∈ add(S1) but P1 ∉ add(S1). The subsequent argument in the paper nevertheless considers a simple submodule S→F and shows F/S is torsion, which is a stronger condition that would suffice, but the stated reduction to 'maximal quotients' is incorrect.

The text cites [1] (survey in Section 3), [2] (Lemma 3.3 and Proposition 3.5), and [3] (Theorem 1.1), but the reference list begins at [4]. Conversely, [4] Crawley-Boevey and [5] Demonet-Iyama-Jasso are listed but never cited in the text. Thus the bibliography is incomplete and inconsistent with the in-text citations.

The abstract claims the result for 'finitely generated modules over an artinian ring', but the Notation section states: 'Throughout the paper, Λ will be a finite-dimensional k-algebra over some field k'. The proof is therefore set up only for finite-dimensional algebras over a field, which are a proper subclass of artinian rings. As written, the abstract states a broader theorem than the body proves.
